input.brief: a research memo for a private expense-tracking iPhone app deciding how an AI assistant should be allowed to read someone's spending

direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: Mosaic masthead, title on axis
hero.blueprint: The top 52% of the viewport is a full-width masthead band built as a gutterless mosaic: a CSS grid of 6 columns and 2 rows in which four cells are photographs (object-fit: cover, all greyscale via filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)) and the rest are flat tiles in two or three palette colours. One photograph spans two columns and one colour tile spans both rows; cells butt together with no gap. The header lies flush on the band's upper edge: the wordmark in a solid ink block at far left, a flat accent-coloured tab holding three text links that runs from the block to 42% of the width, and the single action as a text link at the far right. Below the band, on the paper ground: a standfirst of one sentence at 20px on the 16px left margin, max 30ch, and, starting exactly at 42% of the width, the title on two lines at clamp(64px, 8.3vw, 128px), medium weight, tracking -0.06em, leading 0.9, running to the right margin. The title's first baseline sits about 110px under the band.
hero.mobile: The band becomes a mosaic of 3 columns and 2 rows taking the top 38% of the screen: two photographs and four colour tiles. The header is a single row above it with the wordmark block and a menu word. The axis collapses to the 16px left margin: the title at 13vw on two lines, then the standfirst at 17px beneath it. The action sits as a text link at the foot of the screen.
hero.headline: The title of the report, programme or product, 2-5 words, at most 26 characters across two lines.

type.note: A true didone with hairline serifs and vertical stress over a light geometric sans, the classic fashion-magazine pairing. Suits luxury property, jewellery, fragrance and fashion.

palette.name: Burgundy and bubblegum
palette.note: Deep burgundy is the ground for the whole page and bubblegum pink sets every word on it. The button and the active state of a control are solid pink with burgundy type; product photographs supply any other colour.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Lead line over four columns
sections.blueprint: Two parts on one 12-column grid with 20px margins. First, a lead paragraph of 30–40 words spans all 12 columns at clamp(22px, 2.2vw, 32px), regular weight, leading 1.2: three lines that read as the opening of a text, with no heading before it. 72px below, four equal columns (three grid columns each, 24px gutters) carry small text at 14–15px with leading 1.45. Each column is one paragraph of 40–70 words that opens with a bold run-in phrase of two or three words in full ink, the rest continuing on the same line in the soft ink. Columns top-align and end ragged at different depths. No cards, icons or dividers; the bold run-ins are the only markers. The four columns answer four plain questions: who, what, where, how to reach them. Padding is modest, 96px top and bottom, so a sheet of images can start straight after.
sections.mobile: The lead paragraph at 20px, full width. The four columns become a two-by-two grid with a 20px gutter and 40px row gap at 14px; if any paragraph exceeds 60 words, switch to one column with 32px between paragraphs. Run-in phrases stay bold.

sections.name: Fixed output, live controls
sections.blueprint: A split the reader operates. Left, columns 1–6: a flat colour field that is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh, edge to edge, holding one thing the product makes (a card, an email, a chart, a rendered page) centred at true size, about 420px wide, root marked data-ui. Right, columns 8–12: a reading column no wider than 44ch, with four or five capability blocks 50vh apart. Each block is a sentence at 28–32px, a paragraph at 17px, and directly beneath it one real control at interface size: a slider, a segmented choice, a toggle, a short text field. Operating a control changes the fixed output on the left at once, and changes persist, so by the last block the reader has configured their own. The section heading, two to four words at 40–44px, opens the right column, 72px from the top.
sections.mobile: The output sits in a sticky field at the top, 42svh tall, cropped to its most telling region, not shrunk. Blocks scroll beneath on the page ground: sentence at 22px, paragraph at 16px, control at full width with 44px targets. The field releases after the last block.

sections.name: Plain names in columns
sections.blueprint: A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
sections.mobile: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

sections.name: Stages as one bar
sections.blueprint: The product's progress bar, enlarged until it spans the page, is the diagram. One bar runs across columns 1–12, 22vh tall, built as a flex row of three or four solid segments with 6px gaps, root marked data-ui. Each segment's width follows how long that stage really takes (flex-grow from the true durations, 12% minimum), and each is a different flat palette colour, so the reader sees at once that signing up is a sliver and the rest is the product working. Inside every segment, top-left with 20px padding, its duration in words at clamp(20px, 2vw, 30px): 'Two minutes', 'About a day'. Under each segment, on its left edge, one clause at 17px, 22ch wide, beginning with its order word. Above the bar, 64px clear of it, the heading: two to five words at clamp(48px, 6.4vw, 104px), flush left. Nothing else.
sections.mobile: The bar turns vertical: segments stack as full-width blocks whose heights keep the proportions, 72px minimum, 6px gaps, about 70svh in total. Each holds its duration at 22px top-left and its clause at 16px beneath. The heading sits above at 11vw on two lines.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: The Queue
references.idea: An essay on queueing where the queue is the ornament: a line of drawn figures stands along the bottom of the hero and returns between chapters in changing period dress.
references.hero: Pinkish warm-grey page. A 12px mono breadcrumb sits top-left; there is no other navigation. The two-word title is set in a light serif at 200px (14vw), centred, its middle slightly above the viewport centre, spanning about 60% of the width with tight tracking. One centred line of grey 20px serif sits 40px beneath. The lower third stays empty until a single row of about 25 small greyscale drawn figures, each around 110px tall, stands on a hairline rule 20px above the bottom edge and runs the full width like a frieze.
references.type: Newsreader does everything: Light at 200px with -0.05em tracking for the title, regular near 30px for chapter headings, 18px body with open leading, and pale ghost numerals around 22vw. A monospace appears only in the breadcrumb and footer labels.
references.colour: #ebe4e0 #2b2622 #6f6763 #d9d2ce #16a05a — One warm rosy-grey ground throughout, brown-black text, mid-grey secondary lines, greyscale drawings. A single green appears only in the breadcrumb and one footer button.
references.imagery: Hand-drawn greyscale figures with fine outlines, standing in single file on a hairline; each band changes era costume and spacing. No boxes or backgrounds: figures sit directly on the page colour, full width.
references.layout: After the centred hero, text runs in one narrow column about 40% of the viewport wide, starting 30% from the left; the right third holds only a huge pale chapter numeral. Chapters are separated by full-width bands of figures on hairlines.

sections.description: Chapter block. A 30px serif question heads a text column about 590px wide, offset 30% from the left. Behind it in the top-right corner sits a chapter numeral roughly 22vw tall in a tint barely darker than the page, cropped by the section's top edge. Body is 18px serif at about 1.8 leading; bold run-in phrases open key paragraphs in place of subheads. No pull quotes, side notes or images inside the text.

Divider band between chapters: a full-width strip about 180px tall in which 10 to 15 drawn figures stand at uneven intervals on a 1px rule, with 120px of empty page above. The number and spacing of figures follow the story (few and scattered early, an evenly spaced orderly line later), so the divider carries part of the argument instead of acting as a spacer.

The ending switches voice. A white rounded promo bar with a blue pill button, then a heavy sans heading with a short grey paragraph and one green button, then a hairline, a mono uppercase label, and four small white cards in a row (thumbnail, mono number, bold title). It is narrower than the page and sits on a different axis from the essay column, so it reads as site furniture attached afterwards.

steal: Turn the subject into the section divider: a frieze of small figures on a hairline, redrawn for each chapter, in place of rules or spacers.
Set one serif family at three far-apart sizes (200px title, 30px heading, 18px body) and mark chapters with a pale 22vw numeral cropped off the corner.
Hold body text to a narrow column offset left of centre and leave the right third empty instead of filling it with sidebars.

references.name: Artem Taradash
references.idea: A designer's CV compressed into one newspaper-like band at the top, after which oversized product renders and project artefacts speak at full scale.
references.hero: White page with 20px margins. Top-left are three small black rectangular tags with white text (name and two links). Below them a three-line statement at about 3vw in regular-weight grotesk fills the first third, left-aligned. To its right, starting at the very top edge, run two narrow columns of 12px text, then a third column listing clients one per line, and in the far top-right a circular portrait about 200px wide with a white hand-lettered word across the face. This text band ends by a quarter of the height. Below it a huge cut-out vehicle render bleeds off the bottom, with a project card at right.
references.type: One family, Diatype, in regular weight throughout. Three sizes: about 43px for statements and project titles, 12.4px for all running text, about 11px for tags. Tight leading, sentence case, no bold and no capitals; hierarchy comes from size alone.
references.colour: #ffffff #111111 #f7f9fb #1c4fd8 #f0a23a — Strictly black on white for the frame. All colour arrives with project material: an orange-to-blue gradient, a cobalt zigzag pattern, warm photography.
references.imagery: Product renders cut out on white and shown very large, interface screenshots with a small corner radius, a full-width studio photo with a circular logo overlaid, and textile-pattern fields running margin to margin. Scale varies sharply between projects.
references.layout: A loose six-column grid with 20px margins; small text blocks hang from column lines beside very large images. Each project is arranged differently, and there are no dividers or section backgrounds, only white space and jumps in scale. The tag nav stays fixed top-left.

sections.description: Each project pairs one oversized visual with a small caption cluster. In the first, a cut-out product render fills the left 60% and bleeds off the edge. The right third stacks a landscape screenshot with slightly rounded corners, then a row holding a tiny label and two-line title at about 3vw on the left and a five-line 12px description on the right.

A row of three: a round black watch-face mock-up about a quarter of the width, a wide rectangle filled with a horizontal blue, violet, orange, blue gradient with a tiny tick scale beneath it, and a narrow text column at far right with label, three-line title and two short paragraphs. Circle, rectangle and text share a top line.

A cobalt-and-white zigzag textile pattern runs margin to margin for more than a full viewport height with only a two-line caption beneath it at left. Before it, a black-backed mosaic of pattern samples and report-cover mock-ups sits beside two narrow text columns. The pattern is given a section to itself with no mock-up frame.

Closing row on white: a tiny label, then a four-line sentence at about 3vw in the left third; a small square portrait at the two-thirds mark; to its right a short question with two underlined links below. All three hang from the same top line with empty space between them.

steal: Put bio, client list and portrait in one compact multi-column band at the top so the first scroll is already work.
Use solid black rectangular tags with white text as the only navigation chrome.
Let one project artefact (a pattern, a gradient) run full width for a whole screen with a two-line caption instead of framing it in a mock-up.

references.name: Sharplink
references.idea: A crypto treasury presented as precision hardware: chrome machined parts and glass capsules rendered in 3D on deep blue, overlaid with dashed machine-vision tracking boxes.
references.hero: Full-bleed video of exploded brushed-metal components floating on a navy-to-cobalt gradient, covered by a web of thin white dashed lines and small square tracking markers. Logo top-left on a 2% margin; top-right a segmented strip of five dark rectangular tabs in narrow uppercase plus an arrow square. The headline is top-left, two lines at 6.1vw in regular weight with -0.03em tracking, starting 18% down. Under it two stacked rectangular buttons: white with a blue arrow square attached, then a translucent dark one. Bottom row: a stock-exchange badge at left, a three-line lead paragraph at about 1.3vw starting 26% across, and bottom-right a translucent dark news card about 30% wide.
references.type: Archivo regular for headlines (88px in the hero, about 3vw in sections) and 16px body; Archivo Narrow in bold uppercase with wide tracking for nav, buttons and tiny labels. Headlines never go bold: hierarchy comes from size and from fading inactive items to grey.
references.colour: #050c17 #0e3f97 #e6edf7 #a7a8ab #1f6bff #ffffff — One blue family from near-black navy through cobalt to icy white; sections are vertical blue gradients, light or dark. Bright blue appears only as tiny square markers and arrow buttons; chrome grey from the renders.
references.imagery: Chrome and glass 3D objects (exploded device parts, a spike-tipped capsule holding icons) lit coolly, often with dashed annotation lines or shown as dotted wireframes; full-bleed in the hero, floating free at the right in later sections.
references.layout: 2% margins and square corners everywhere. Sections are full-viewport gradient fields with a headline at left and a 3D object or data card at right; lists run as label, title and paragraph in two columns. Tiny blue square bullets mark section starts.

sections.description: Light icy-gradient section. A two-line headline in grey-blue at about 3vw at the left, with a small paragraph far below it at bottom-left. Centre: a tall 3:4 card with a navy-to-cobalt vertical gradient, a tiny uppercase label, a rising line chart over a faint dotted grid, and a full-width dark button at its base. Right third: three faint, nearly transparent rows, each with a small numbered tag, one line of text and a ghosted line drawing.

Pinned list beside a 3D object. Left 60%: stacked rows, each with a tiny uppercase label, a two-line title at about 1.3vw in a first column and a short paragraph in a second column starting 26% across. Only the active row is at full contrast; the rest are dimmed to roughly 40%. Right 40%: a chrome-and-glass capsule about 80% of the viewport tall whose interior icon changes per row. The ground shifts from icy white to deep cobalt partway through.

A black panel inset by 2% on a navy ground with small blue square markers at its corners. Logo mark top-left; a two-line statement at about 2vw at the left, first line white and second line grey; two rectangular buttons below. A dotted wireframe version of the capsule fills the right half. Under the panel, a tiny uppercase label at left and a small button at right.

Cobalt gradient footer: a newsletter line with an underlined email field at left, three small link columns across the middle and right, exchange badge and legal microtext below. The wordmark closes the page in letters spanning the full width, cropped by the bottom edge and fading from white at the top to transparent.

steal: Overlay a 3D render with thin dashed lines and tiny square markers linking its parts, as if a vision system were tracking the object.
Build buttons as square-cornered rectangles with a separate coloured arrow square attached to the right edge.
In a pinned list beside a 3D object, dim every row except the active one and change what sits inside the object for each row.
references.media: A full-bleed 12s loop of 3D chrome and glass objects covers the whole fold, with text docked in the four corners straight on it. Below: a 3D capsule pinned in the right third while a list of claims scrolls on the left, its inner emblem swapping per row, a dark card sliding over it that turns the covered part into a dashed wireframe, a sticky portrait video of chrome pipes at the right edge, and a full-width wordmark canvas cropped by the bottom of the viewport; square corners throughout.
references.motion: The hero is composed at 400ms with the video playing and no preloader (load 21.3s), and Lenis runs four pins over fixed layers: one fixed gradient layer behind everything crossfades the grounds, the capsule stays pinned across three sections as each claim brightens from about 40% to full, and the manifesto fills character by character (423 split characters). The workhorse ease is cubic-bezier(.455,.03,.515,.955), on 57 observed opacity, background and colour transitions at .25-.3s.
